title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Employees
tiers.description: Employees who are not Designated Persons. Only restriction is the insider trading prohibition on dealing while in possession of inside information; the Black Out Period, clearance and Key Management Personnel hedging prohibition do not apply to this tier.

tiers.name: Designated Person
tiers.description: A Director or person having authority for planning, directing and controlling the activities of the Company, directly or indirectly, whether as an employee or consultant, and any other person notified by the Company that they are deemed a designated person. Subject to Black Out Periods and must obtain prior written clearance from a Clearance Officer before dealing in Company Securities, and must take reasonable steps to prevent dealing by Associated Persons.

tiers.name: Key Management Personnel
tiers.description: A person having authority and responsibility for planning, directing and controlling the activities of the Company, directly or indirectly, including any Director (whether executive or otherwise). Separately defined from Designated Person; subject to the hedging prohibition in clause 15 on remuneration that is unvested or vested but subject to a holding lock.

tiers.name: Associated Persons
tiers.description: Includes family or nominee companies and family trusts of a Designated Person, and any investment manager acting on their behalf or on behalf of an associated person. A Designated Person must take all reasonable and necessary steps to prevent dealing by Associated Persons when the Designated Person may not deal.

definitions.hedging_definition: an arrangement with anyone if that arrangement would have the effect of limiting the exposure of the member to risk relating to an element of the member's remuneration that: (a) has not vested in the member; or (b) has vested in the member but remains subject to a holding lock

windows.start_anchor: the last day of the financial year (currently 30 June)
windows.end_anchor: the second trading day after the public announcement of the financial results of the year

windows.start_anchor: the last day of the half financial year (currently 31 December)
windows.end_anchor: the second trading day after the public announcement of the half yearly financial results of the half year

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Company may notify additional Black Out Periods from time to time, for example where it is considering a major transaction that could have a material effect on the stock price. The Policy does not state whether such periods, or the reasons for them, are confidential.

exemption_authority: Exceptional-circumstances clearance to sell during a Black Out Period may be given by a Clearance Officer for severe financial hardship or court order/enforceable undertaking, or by the Chairman (or the Board if the Chairman is involved) for any other circumstances deemed exceptional (clause 10). No broader waiver authority is stated.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Company Securities includes shares, debentures, rights, options and any other financial products of the Company traded on any stock exchange.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An OTC put and call written by a bank are neither 'of the Company' nor 'traded on any stock exchange', so on a literal reading they are not 'Company Securities' and the Policy's Dealing, Black Out Period and clearance regime does not apply to them at all, outside the separate Key Management Personnel hedging prohibition.

bespoke_clauses.topic: no margin lending or secured financing prohibition
bespoke_clauses.clause: a disposal of Company Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike most ASX-listed peer policies, this Policy contains no prohibition on margin lending, granting security over, or otherwise financing against Company Securities; this excluded-trading carve-out for a secured lender's forced sale positively assumes such arrangements exist and are lawful, so the loan leg of a funded collar is not restricted by this Policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A member of the Key Management Personnel must not enter into an arrangement with anyone if that arrangement would have the effect of limiting the exposure of the member to risk relating to an element of the member's remuneration that: (a) has not vested in the member; or (b) has vested in the member but remains subject to a holding lock.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is broader than the 'Company Securities' Dealing regime (it catches any arrangement with anyone, not just exchange-traded Company Securities) and would catch an OTC collar over unvested or holding-locked equity remuneration, but it does not reach vested, unrestricted shares.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Notwithstanding clauses 9(a) and 9(c) but subject to clause 9(b), the following types of trading are excluded from the operation of this policy: ... a disposal of Company Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A lender's enforcement sale of the collared shares is excluded from the Black Out Period and clearance requirements (though it remains subject to the insider trading prohibition in clause 9(b)), giving the bank a clear enforcement path even during a closed period.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This form is valid for a period of three business days from the date of approval.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A cleared collar trade must be priced and executed within 3 business days of approval, a tight window for documenting an OTC derivative with a bank.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Key Management Personnel means a person having authority and responsibility for planning, directing and controlling the activities of the Company... Designated Person means a Director or person having authority for planning, directing and controlling the activities of the Company...
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The two defined terms are nearly identical but not declared coextensive; in practice the same director or executive is likely both a Designated Person (subject to Black Out Periods and clearance) and a member of Key Management Personnel (subject to the separate hedging ban), so both regimes need to be checked for any individual counterparty.

summary: A funded collar is comparatively unrestricted under this Policy. 'Company Securities' is defined narrowly as financial products of Mader itself traded on a stock exchange, so an OTC put and call written by a bank arguably fall outside the Dealing, Black Out Period and clearance regime altogether, except that Key Management Personnel are separately and broadly banned from any arrangement that limits their exposure to risk on remuneration that is unvested or still subject to a holding lock. Once shares have vested and any holding lock has lifted, there is no hedging restriction at all, and clearance under clause 11 (a 3-business-day approval from a Clearance Officer, outside Black Out Periods and absent inside information) would only be needed if the derivative or its underlying were treated as a 'Company Security'. Critically, the Policy contains no prohibition whatsoever on margin lending, granting security over Company Securities, or other secured financing; the only reference to secured lending is an excluded-trading carve-out that lets a secured lender's forced sale proceed even during a Black Out Period. On this reading, a funded collar over vested, unrestricted shares held by a Designated Person or Key Management Personnel member is achievable with comparatively few conditions, though the absence of any 'substance over form' clause leaves some residual risk that the Company could still seek to apply the Policy's spirit to a bespoke derivative referencing its shares.
